title: REA and ten repositories for NBRT cybersecurity workflow research
status: Initial source assessment; exhaustive line-by-line audit remains incomplete
scope: Public repositories, local source inspection only. No tools installed, targets scanned, samples executed, or live systems modified.
nbrt_context: Resolved from repository README: NBRET, Network Based Reverse Engineering Tool. Engagement types remain to be selected.
selection: Ten curated related or distinctive repositories, not a global popularity ranking.

repositories.learning: Provider-neutral observations, explicit confidence and authority, preserved upstream caveats, artifact digests, and residual unknowns.
repositories.proposal: Investigation records that connect artifact identity, suspected weakness, evidence, validation experiment, and remediation regression.
repositories.limitations: Source review does not establish real-provider behavior. Windows Ghidra support is explicitly experimental and narrower than general cross-platform support. Local analysis does not make the connected model local or establish isolation.

repositories.learning: Persistent program-bound decompiler interface, explicit completion checks, process recovery.
repositories.proposal: Repeatable headless analysis of owned native software and comparisons across releases.
repositories.limitations: Decompiled pseudocode is a reconstruction; engine correctness and architecture coverage need target-specific validation.

repositories.learning: The release repository delegates implementation to separate core, gum, language binding, and tooling repositories; interceptor state includes transactions and per-thread invocation context.
repositories.proposal: Validate narrowly defined runtime hypotheses in disposable lab instances.
repositories.limitations: Instrumentation can change timing and behavior. Main repository review alone cannot cover implementation.

repositories.learning: Language-neutral AST pattern matching preserves metavariables and source ranges; scan orchestration is distinct from matching.
repositories.proposal: Convert a confirmed source-level weakness into a reviewed rule with positive and negative fixtures.
repositories.limitations: Pattern matches are not exploitability proof; commercial engine capabilities must be distinguished from this repository.

repositories.learning: Separate protocol/headless concurrency and per-template lifecycle callbacks; failed origin-scoped attempts should not suppress later attempts.
repositories.proposal: Versioned approved checks with target scope, rate budgets, and lifecycle receipts.
repositories.limitations: Templates vary in side effects; scanner output needs independent confirmation and pinned template provenance.

repositories.learning: Ability selection uses agent capabilities and operation facts; sequential and batch execution have different stop-check granularity; cleanup links are generated separately.
repositories.proposal: Bounded purple-team exercises with expected telemetry and explicit stopping conditions.
repositories.limitations: Generated cleanup is not proof that cleanup completed. Batch behavior can delay stopping-condition checks. Plugin submodules were not recursively inspected.

repositories.learning: Tests carry stable identities, platforms, arguments, prerequisites, executors, and optional cleanup.
repositories.proposal: Detection coverage matrix that distinguishes selected, executed, observed, alerted, investigated, and cleaned-up tests.
repositories.limitations: Even one technique file mixes simple discovery with tests that download external code; technique ID alone is not an adequate scope or risk boundary.

repositories.learning: Separate generation, probes, detectors, and evaluators; unscored outputs are counted separately from passes; plugin metadata and attempt identity are retained.
repositories.proposal: Independent evaluation of agent boundary failures with preserved attempts and uncertainty.
repositories.limitations: Detector scores are measurements under a rubric, not confirmed real-world vulnerabilities. Some components require external models or services.

repositories.role: Application-level AI regression and red-team evaluation
repositories.learning: Separate test plugins, strategies, providers, and assertions. Remote generation selection depends on credentials, cloud login, endpoints, and flags.
repositories.proposal: Agent tests for untrusted document instructions, cross-tenant access, inappropriate tool calls, and canary-data leakage, scored against tool traces and deterministic assertions.
repositories.limitations: Local CLI installation does not ensure local processing. Model-judge agreement alone is insufficient evidence; review data flow and costs before real cases.

repositories.learning: Validate command sequences and preserve distinctions between workflow completion, retry, and unprocessed updates.
repositories.proposal: Long-running engagements that survive restarts and retain approval and result history.
repositories.limitations: Retryable workflows need idempotent external activities; durability is not automatic permission to repeat an action. Running a service introduces operational cost.

repositories.learning: Explicit node subscriptions, writes, retries, timeouts, checkpoint versions and pending writes. Delta-channel retention can depend on ancestor history.
repositories.proposal: Branching investigations with review interrupts and replayable state; borrow state design before adopting another orchestration framework.
repositories.limitations: Checkpoints are not a sandbox. Naive checkpoint pruning can break delta reconstruction; persistence adapters and serializer policy require separate review.

proposed_pilots.name: Finding to regression
proposed_pilots.flow: Owned artifact -> REA investigation -> independently confirmed finding -> reviewed Semgrep or Nuclei check -> regression fixtures -> retest after remediation
proposed_pilots.measure: Analyst time, reproducibility, false positives, and whether the fixed version passes while the vulnerable fixture fails.

proposed_pilots.name: Agent boundary evaluation
proposed_pilots.flow: Synthetic untrusted input -> agent in lab -> tool-call and data-access receipts -> deterministic policy checks -> promptfoo regression and independent garak comparison
proposed_pilots.measure: Unauthorized tool calls, synthetic canary disclosure, benign-task success, repeated-run failure frequency, cost.

proposed_pilots.name: Detection evidence matrix
proposed_pilots.flow: Selected reviewed Atomic tests -> disposable instrumented endpoints -> optional CALDERA scenario -> telemetry collection -> alert and cleanup verification
proposed_pilots.measure: Execution success separately from telemetry visibility, alert generation, investigation time, and verified cleanup.

adoption_order: Choose one NBRT use case and a known-answer lab fixture
Benchmark REA against an existing CLI workflow on the same question
Preserve evidence and build one regression test
Add orchestration only after the small workflow is useful
